Average Joes: Nobody's picked their keepers for the upcoming draft yet, so the question is which two players on this roster are actually worth it. Drake London and Garrett Wilson are the obvious answers — London's a true WR1 even at a round-one cost, and Wilson's the bargain of the two at a sixth-round price. After that it drops off fast: Jameson Williams is next in line, but he was also a round-one pick, so keeping him wouldn't be cheap either. There's no hidden third option here. With most of the league sitting on a spare valuable keeper or two, this is a team that should be offering up a 2026 pick to pry one loose rather than expecting extras of its own — Trevor Lawrence or Zach Charbonnet (both Jack of All Trades) and Zay Flowers or Tee Higgins (Surfin' Loons) are the kind of names worth calling about.
Crusty Baguettes: Ladd McConkey (a massive bargain at a seventh-round cost) and Cam Ward headline the keeper options here, but there's real depth behind them too — Chuba Hubbard, Rico Dowdle and Wan'Dale Robinson are all legitimate value plays that won't fit into just two slots. That's a genuine sell-one-keep-one situation at running back or receiver. The move is shopping whichever of that trio doesn't get kept while the price is still good — and on the buy side, The SHIELD's Tyler Warren (a TE1 they can only keep two of three good options for) is a realistic target if a Hubbard-or-Dowdle package gets the call started.
Draft A Better Team Tom: Rashee Rice at an eleventh-round cost is one of the best-value keeper options in the league, and Sam Darnold gives them a legitimate second. Behind that pair it gets thinner — D'Andre Swift and Courtland Sutton are fine depth pieces, not the kind of value that forces a hard choice. The real asset here is draft capital: the No. 1 overall pick in 2026. Rather than hope the draft solves everything, pairing that pick with a role player to buy a proven keeper option from a deeper roster is the higher-probability play — Chase Brown or Marvin Harrison Jr. (Minnesota Muskies) are both sitting behind an even better top-of-roster and could be had.
Jack of All Trades: This is one of the deepest keeper situations in the league. Jaxon Smith-Njigba at a sixth-round cost is arguably the single best value keeper anywhere, and Bucky Irving isn't far behind at an eleventh-round price — that's the obvious top two. But Trevor Lawrence, a legitimate starting QB1, is sitting third, and Zach Charbonnet gives them a fourth strong option at running back. With only two slots to use, both are tradeable. Two natural buyers: Average Joes or Tank U, Next for Lawrence (both are QB-needy), and Average Joes or Draft A Better Team Tom for Charbonnet.
Middle School Mayhem: De'Von Achane and George Pickens are both outstanding value at their keeper costs — a seventh-round running back and an eighth-round receiver who both play like top-15 assets at their position. That pair alone makes this a strong roster. Behind them, Michael Pittman and Dallas Goedert are solid depth without forcing a real decision, so the keeper calculus is genuinely just picking between Achane and Pickens for a change, not shopping a third star. Worth reaching out to and the Giant Peach or Draft A Better Team Tom about their draft capital in exchange for depth, since neither of those rosters has anything close to this pair.
Minnesota Muskies: This is the deepest keeper situation in the league, full stop. Jaxson Dart at an eleventh-round cost, Chase Brown at a sixth, Marvin Harrison Jr., Sam LaPorta at an eighth, and Jordan Addison are all legitimate keeper-caliber assets — that's five real options for two slots. Whatever doesn't get kept is immediately one of the better trade chips available in the league. Draft A Better Team Tom and Middle School Mayhem are the two teams with the least behind their own top pair, and both would benefit from offering picks for Chase Brown or Sam LaPorta rather than hoping the draft delivers equivalent value.
Moran’s Also-Rans: Colston Loveland and Emeka Egbuka are tied as the top value options here, but Jordan Love (a tenth-round-caliber value at an eighth-round cost) and Brian Thomas Jr. are right behind them — four real keeper-quality assets for two slots. That's a clear surplus, and either the quarterback or the extra receiver is worth shopping rather than losing to the pool for nothing. Middle School Mayhem and Tank U, Next are both thinner at the position level and should be the first calls about Love or Thomas Jr., ideally using some of the 16 picks already on their 2026 board as the base of a return.
My Name Is: TreVeyon Henderson, Breece Hall and Rome Odunze are all bunched together as this roster's top value, which is an unusual problem to have — three players worth keeping and only two slots. On top of that, Tucker Kraft at a thirteenth-round cost might be the single best value keeper in the entire league, a top-10 tight end for pocket change. Whichever of the RB/WR trio doesn't get kept, plus a look at moving Kraft or Quentin Johnston, gives this team real trade leverage. Tank U, Next and and the Giant Peach are both light on proven skill talent and should be calling about it.
Seal Team Nix: Bo Nix and Chris Olave are quality building blocks at their (round-one) cost, but the real value plays are Kyren Williams at an eleventh-round price and Baker Mayfield at an eighth — both massive bargains relative to what they're actually worth. That's four legitimate keeper options for two slots, which makes this one of the better-positioned rosters in the league heading into keeper decisions. Tank U, Next and Middle School Mayhem are the natural buyers for Mayfield or Williams, and either should come with real draft capital attached given the price these two are currently costing to keep.
Surfin' Loons: Brock Bowers at a fifth-round cost is a top-five dynasty tight end for a mid-round price — one of the best individual value keepers in the league. Behind him, Tetairoa McMillan, Zay Flowers, Tee Higgins and Jaylen Waddle are four legitimate WR1-caliber options, all at a round-one cost, which means none of them are cheap but all of them are keepable. Two slots can't cover Bowers plus three of those four, so this is a rare case of trading away pure talent rather than a value play. Average Joes and Draft A Better Team Tom, both light at receiver, are the obvious first calls.
Tank U, Next: Drake Maye at an eighth-round cost and Kyle Pitts at a twelfth are both exceptional value — a top-five dynasty quarterback and a difference-making tight end for next to nothing. Kyler Murray gives them a real third option at a fifth-round price, which is the one piece worth shopping since only two slots are in play. The problem is everything after that: Aaron Jones and Alvin Kamara are both late in their careers, and there's a real cliff beyond the top three. Moving Murray for a young skill piece is the play — Kyren Williams (Seal Team Nix) or Rome Odunze / Quentin Johnston (My Name Is) are worth calling about.
The Flying Kites: Running back is loaded here — Omarion Hampton, Quinshon Judkins and Blake Corum are all legitimate keeper-caliber assets, with Judkins in particular an outstanding value at a tenth-round cost. Nico Collins adds a strong receiver option too. That's at least three real keepers for two slots, with the extra running back the clear trade chip. and the Giant Peach and Crusty Baguettes are both thinner at the position and should be the first calls about Judkins or Corum, ideally with a 2026 pick attached given how cheap that production currently costs to keep.
The SHIELD: Puka Nacua at an eleventh-round cost might be the single best value keeper in the entire league — a top-10 dynasty asset for a price that low is essentially free. Amon-Ra St. Brown isn't far behind at a ninth-round price. Behind that pair, Tyler Warren and Javonte Williams are both real, tradeable value on their own — this roster has four keeper-caliber assets for two slots. Crusty Baguettes and Middle School Mayhem are both light at the positions where Warren and Williams play, and either would be smart to offer draft capital for one of them before it's too late.
and the Giant Peach: Cam Skattebo, Jayden Reed and Brenton Strange are all solid value at their keeper costs, but none of them is the kind of true difference-maker other rosters are sitting on — this is a roster with useful depth and no obvious star to build around. Skattebo and Reed are the likely top two; Strange and Woody Marks are shoppable pieces rather than must-keeps. With a 2026 first-rounder and two second-round picks on the board, the better move is packaging that draft capital with the extra depth to trade up for a real difference-maker — The SHIELD's Tyler Warren or Surfin' Loons' spare WR1 are the kind of targets worth the ask.
